title: USBHID: Support extended usages in descriptors
description:
Usage, Usage Minimum and Usage Maximum can be "Extended" Usages. When
parsing report descriptor, respect page encoded in extended usage value.

Remove arbitrary usage count limit, as the usage ranges are limited to
16-bit value and thus the usages array can grow by up by 256 KiB with
single usage range.

notes.body: @berkakinci and @FFY00 could you please review it?
Good idea handling extended usages.  I looked through quickly; I'll have to revisit tomorrow morning.

I think the main point of extended usages is exactly to support this. Do you have a device that uses them, or are you just adding this for completeness?
Personally, I haven't ever seen extended usages used in the wild, and I would guess if I did, it would be to override the active usage page. The reason I left this out originally was for simplicity, as properly supporting extended usages would require a biggish amount of complexity added, I think.

I think the reason is to allow declaring item from different page without changing usage page. That is, you declare "main usage page" as global, but if you have just one or two items from different pages (especially in the middle of report), you don't change the global page. While the implementation allows only items from same page, this is a step forward for supporting items with different usage pages (such items don't sound sensible to me).

The real reason behind this change are malformed captures that cause issues like #17165. Single min/max spanning across multiple pages does not make any sense. This change indirectly limits (to IMHO sensible amounts) the memory malformed captures take, while rejecting outright faulty ones.

While the arbitrary limit is better than nothing (!1810), something that takes into account what the 32-bit values in Usage, Usage Minimum and Usage Maximum mean, sounds better and easier to maintain in the long run.
In fact, I am wrong about it, see Berk Akinci example below.

Here's a more authoritative example of a touch screen; at least how MS wants it: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/component-guidelines/touchscreen-sample-report-descriptors

The trace I attached was just a cheap touch "overlay" device from the wild.

There is something else that bothers me.  The spec isn't explicit if the usage page in the extended usage affects the global state.  I.e. do any following usages belong to the previous usage page or the one mentioned in the latest extended usage?  My guess is the intent is these are temporary, and don't affect global state.  I didn't find it spelled out explicitly.

May be this lack of detail is the reason it's not seen in the wild by @FFY00.

I think it is explicit about it not affecting the global state, as it would be a local item. At most, you could argue that it modifies the following entries for the current main item. But, among other things, the spec says "Extended usages can be used to override the currently defined Usage Page for individual usages.", emphasis on *for individual usages*.

The code overall looks good anyway :blush:
resolved all threads

Are these usage_page assertions about usages within a delimited set of alternative usages?  (HID v1.11 Top of page 42)

If they're within a collection, having usages from different pages is "normal."   For example digitizer page doesn't have X and Y usages, but they're taken from the "Generic Desktop Controls" page.

In any case, this code interferes with the (poorly) parsed HID Data in my trace.  It's not parsing at all any more.
I tried skipping these checks, but I couldn't restore the HID Data parsing.  So may be unrelated.

See attached.  Look at any of the HID data in the Interrupt In packets.

[MultiTouch_1-10_fingers.pcapng](/uploads/55c9c6c2dd28962e6f2f4feb66fccdb3/MultiTouch_1-10_fingers.pcapng)

They're not within a collection, we actually do not save any data related to collections as it is unecessary to parse. Collection data might be useful for a more high-level interpretation, like the OS deciding to have some custom handling for touch inputs to interact with the system, which it may want to be different than what it does with mice. Since we are only interested in interpreting the raw data, we do not need them. It would be interesting to add the collection details to the items, but that'd only be a small nice-to have IMO.

IIRC the groupings are per main item, so the assert should be fine. I don't have time to look at your capture right now, so I don't know what is going wrong there, sorry. Perhaps I will have some time later, if Tomasz needs a hand.

What we should probably do is remove the item groups in favor of actual data entries. This was the first HID parser I wrote, so I was not exactly sure how to structure it and this end up being a design oversight.
I have a better structured parser at https://github.com/usb-tools/python-hid-parser, which does not have this design issues. The differences are that it is fully dynamic -- it dissects the data based on the usage type, instead of having custom per-page dissection routines -- and that it splits into actual data fields internally.

> The differences are that it is fully dynamic -- it dissects the data based on the usage type, instead of having custom per-page dissection routines

I was also thinking the per-page dissectors were manual/cumbersome and unnecessary.  I haven't looked at your Python parser yet.  I was thinking if we added something like a "data type" to the usage arrays in the code, all interpretation would be common code from then on.

[Edit]
... And now that I've quickly browsed through the Python, I see that's exactly what you've done there.
```
class GenericDesktopControls(_Data):
    POINTER = 0x01, 'Pointer', UsageTypes.CP
```
Too bad I just copy-pasted the whole usage table spec 1.22 and discarded the data types in post-processing.  May be _someone_ can attempt that again with a PDF parser and less copy-pasting.

If we are putting different usage pages in the same item, this assumption is no longer correct.

Let's create a new inner loop that will get the feature page of the entry and call the dissection functions based on that. This means that we should remove the data loop from the dissection functions, and perhaps just replace it with an index.

Yes, also the assertions within individual code pages will fail. Restructuring would change how vendor data are parsed, as currently it just assumes all usages within `hid_field_t` form single vendor data.

I don't quite know how exactly to structure the loop. The HID_MAIN_TYPE should be checked here, not in individual pages, right?

> If we are putting different usage pages in the same item, this assumption is no longer correct.

And so using `field->usage_page` was never correct. The code simply didn't care that the items could be from different pages, but treated them as if they were from the last global usage page set during `hid_field_t` processing. Extended usages were simply doomed for being treated as unknowns (even if they were from the globally set usage page).

@FFY00 I think I understand the arrays now, but is it that the current array handling in `dissect_usb_hid_keyboard_page()` is basically wrong? That is, it works only by coincidence that multiple keyboards declare arrays where array indexes correspond to usage IDs within keyboard page.

Could you please confirm if the following is true for array fields:
- logical minimum defines the value that corresponds to index 0 in `hid_field_t` `usages` array (e.g. logical minimum equal to 1 means that if 1 is in report, then it means `usages[0]`),
- logical maximum defines the maximum expected value (and `maximum - minimum + 1` should equal `usages` count),
- report size defines how many bits are used to represent the value (and should be atleast `log2(maximum - minimum + 1)`)
- report count defines how many items will appear in array.

Is it possible for logical minimum to be value other than 0 or 1? For example if logical minimum is 3, does it simply mean that value 3 means `usages[0]`?

If the sanity limits mentioned above (`log2(maximum - minimum + 1) >= report size` and `maximum - minimum + 1 == len(usages)`) are not fulfilled then report can still be used, only some values won't be able to be represented?
